title: The three-year retreat
hookLine: Kagyu and other schools keep retreats of three years and three fortnights

lines: A DOOR CLOSES ON A RETREAT HOUSE.
A BELL BEFORE DAWN, EVERY DAY.
cards: A door closes behind a small group of people in maroon robes. On the other side is a plain retreat house: a shrine room, a kitchen, narrow rooms, a walled garden. Outside, friends and family wave.
Inside, a bell rings before dawn, and a schedule begins that will run, day after day, through every season. Nobody inside will come out for a holiday or a wedding.
When the door opens again, the people walking out will have spent three years and three fortnights at it. Today: the three-year retreat.

teach.b: First, the length. Tradition sets the retreat at three years and three fortnights, a little more than three years. Kagyu teachers keep it, and so do other Tibetan schools.
Different teachers give different reasons for the extra fortnights. What matters is that the time is fixed in advance and kept, not shortened when it gets hard. Second, what happens inside.

teach.h: A DAY OF SESSIONS, BEFORE DAWN.
teach.b: The day runs from before dawn into the night in sessions of practice: prostrations, mantra, visualization, the teachings of the lineage, in the order a teacher lays out.
Retreatants cook, clean, and keep silence for long stretches. Some Kagyu retreats include training in the practices that came down from Naropa. Third, why so long.

The Kagyu school prizes practice over learning about practice: Naropa putting down his books to find the meaning, Milarepa going into the mountains and staying there. The long retreat puts that into a calendar.
A teaching heard once becomes a teaching lived through every season.
Fourth, the people who come out. Some go on to teach, which is part of how the whispered lineage keeps passing. Others return to their families and jobs, and carry it quietly.
These retreats are kept in Tibet, India and Nepal, and in Europe and North America too.

This week ran from the light of the Pure Land through the diamond vehicle, three vehicles at once, the ancient ones, hidden treasure and the whispered lineage. Today: a door, closed on purpose, for a long time.

how: In the Kagyu and other Tibetan schools, practitioners enter a closed retreat of three years and three fortnights, following a daily schedule of practice sessions from before dawn into the night under a retreat teacher.

practice: You don't need three years, only one small practice you could keep every day, even on your worst day: this short sit, a single bow in the morning, one breath before you eat. Choose it now, and say it to yourself once, plainly.
Then do it for the length of this sit, as day one.

wordCard.voice: The three-year retreat. A Tibetan retreat of three years and three fortnights, kept by the Kagyu and other schools, with practice from before dawn into the night. Today's word.

orig.note: Tibetan: lo sum chok sum, three years, three fortnights, the name of the retreat.
